title: Steer the Ship
description: EEG dataset from 21 participants performing a continuous control task in which they steered a ship, shown as a rotating arrow, toward a target using left and right key presses. The underlying dynamics were unstable, based on the pole-and-cart problem. Participants were cued before each round about the level of controller noise and environmental noise (wind), giving four noise conditions. Event triggers mark cues, round start, button presses, crashes, successes, and points display.
methods_description: Participants pressed the 'f' and 'j' keys to apply clockwise or counterclockwise angular force to keep the ship oriented toward a target. Rounds lasted up to 1 minute and ended early if the ship crashed. Points were awarded by mean distance to target. Four conditions crossed controller noise and environmental noise (none, environmental only, controller only, both). Event triggers were recorded with EEG.
